Sde394f26The original: NIFTY 50 market filter, 0.5R time stop13.7%−27%First choice, kept for comparison
  • Entry: monthly StochRSI pullback; close above EMA 61 on monthly, weekly and daily; RSI above 50; NIFTY 500 index above its 200-day average (previous close).
  • Exits: stop at the previous week's low; sell at the next open if the trade is not 0.25R up 25 days after entry; otherwise hold until the weekly Supertrend(10, 3) turns from bullish to bearish after entry (sold at the next open). A trade bought while it is already bearish is held until it turns bullish and then bearish, or until the stop or time stop. No holding cap.
  • Sizing: 1% risk per trade on current equity, 10 slots; no position above 20% of equity when bought, and trimmed to 20% at month end; halve size at a 10% drawdown, pause 21 days at 15%. Idle cash in a liquid fund. No NIFTY futures hedges.
  • The worst drawdown (May–June 2006 crash) can't be cut by an entry filter; plan for about −25% to −30%. Expect long losing streaks (29 in a row in the backtest): about 1 trade in 4 wins.

  • SQN 1.9 on Tharp's 100-trade basis (1.6–1.9 poor but tradable, 2–2.4 average, 2.5–2.9 good, 3–5 excellent); 3.8 on all 410 trades. Expectancy +2.32R, std dev of R 12.3R. Sa1f19d11: SQN 2.0, expectancy +2.53R.
  • Low SQN, high expectancy: a few huge winners (best 137R) widen the R spread. Without the 10 best trades expectancy is +0.61R, still positive; missing big winners is the main risk.
  • Market types: bull days and quiet sideways days earn almost all the R; volatile sideways markets are the bleed (negative expectancy), and the NIFTY 500 filter keeps the strategy mostly out of bear markets (few trades, near-flat returns).
  • Each day typed from NIFTY 50 up to the previous close: 13-week change above +5% bull, below −5% bear; volatile if 20-day volatility is above its rolling 3-year median. Trades filed by their entry day.

  • Prices are actual traded prices (adjusted for splits and bonuses, not dividends); dividend income is not counted.
  • Most universes are today's index members, so those results carry survivorship bias and are optimistic. Universe NIFTY500_PIT uses historical NIFTY 500 membership rebuilt from NSE's change notices and is the most realistic.
  • Costs: Sharekhan delivery fees (~0.47% per side) plus 0.1% slippage per side. Risk is a % of starting capital unless the strategy compounds (risk on current equity; see its PDF).
  • Gaps fill at the open; stop is checked before target on the same day. Tax is not deducted.
  • Red: negative return, drawdown worse than 40%, or costs over half the gross profit. Green: CAGR ≥ 8% or CAGR/DD ≥ 0.2.
  • Research and education only, not investment advice. Generated 22 Nov 2026 by site.py.

Glossary

ID
Permanent strategy ID: 'S' + a UUIDv7, shown by its last 8 characters (hover for the full ID). It never changes when a strategy is renamed or edited, and is never reused. Full list: strategies/registry.csv.
Strategy
The setup tested (family) and the variant of its rules. Hover over a name for the full rules.
Universe
The stocks the strategy could trade: today's NIFTY 500 or NIFTY 50 members.
Exit
How winners are closed. 'Target X%' sells when price rises X% above entry. 'No target' holds until the trend exit (a close below EMA61 on the signal timeframe) or the stop. Every trade also has a stop loss.
Risk %
Rupees risked per trade (entry minus stop, times quantity) as a % of starting capital. Most runs use 1%.
Slots
Maximum number of open trades at once. Most runs use 8.
Market filter
'NIFTY > 200-DMA' means no new trades are opened while NIFTY 50 closed below its 200-day simple moving average the day before (BSE Sensex is used before mid-2008, when NIFTY data starts). Open trades are not sold by the filter. 'none' means no market filter.
Win %
Share of closed trades that made money after fees and slippage. A high win rate alone means little: read it together with Avg win %, Avg loss % and Payoff.
Avg trade %
Average net return per closed trade, on the money put into that trade.
Avg trade ₹
Average net profit or loss per closed trade in rupees. Unlike the %, it reflects position size.
Avg win %
Average net return of the winning trades only.
Avg loss %
Average net return of the losing trades only. Usually close to the stop distance plus costs.
Payoff
Average win divided by average loss. A payoff of 3 means the typical winner is three times the typical loser. Low win rates need high payoffs to make money.
Expectancy R
Average net profit per rupee risked. 1R is the planned loss if the stop is hit (about ₹1,000 here). +0.5R means each trade earns half of what it risks on average; below 0 the strategy loses money.
SQN
Van Tharp's System Quality Number = average R ÷ standard deviation of R × √(number of trades, capped at 100). It measures how consistently a system earns its expectancy. 1.6–1.9 poor but tradable, 2–2.4 average, 2.5–2.9 good, 3–5 excellent. Trend systems with a few huge winners score low despite high expectancy.
CAGR %
Compound annual growth rate: the steady yearly return that would turn ₹1 lakh into the final equity.
Max DD %
Maximum drawdown: the largest fall from an equity peak to a later low. The pain you must sit through.
CAGR / DD
CAGR divided by the size of the max drawdown. Return per unit of pain; higher is better. Useful for ranking strategies with different risk.
Trades
Number of closed trades. Fewer than about 100 means the result rests on a small sample.
Trades / yr
Closed trades per year: how busy the strategy keeps you, and how often you pay costs.
Max losing streak
Most losing trades in a row (ordered by exit date). Expect a streak at least this long again.
Median days
Median holding period in calendar days. Under 365 days, gains are taxed as short-term (20%); over 365 days as long-term (12.5%). Tax is not deducted in these results.
Deployed %
Average share of the account held in open positions. The rest sits idle as cash.
Skipped
Signals not taken because all 8 slots were full or cash ran out. Many skips mean the result depends on which signals got the slots (here: tightest stop first).
Costs % of gross
Fees and slippage as a share of profit before costs. Above 100% (or '>100') means the strategy would make money before costs but loses after them.
Report
Link to the full PDF report: rules, equity and drawdown charts, and all results for that strategy.
